analysis.title: Stock Buybacks Have A Lot Of Work To Do To Counter New Issuance
key_insights: Net US equity supply in Q2 2026 was the highest on record, at over $150 billion.
In almost every quarter back to the late 1990s, net equity supply has been negative, because M&A and especially buybacks outweighed secondary issuance and IPOs. That pattern has reversed this year.
Meta's new stock offering and Anthropic's upcoming IPO add to equity supply, which the author calls a structural headwind for the stock market.
Hyperscalers see a need for capital to build out compute capacity. They are turning to equity financing in addition to debt, especially as debt issuance becomes more expensive.
Unlisted firms increasingly want access to public-market funding. Anthropic's IPO is set to exceed the previous record-sized IPO, SpaceX's in the summer.
Buybacks are continuing. Firms that remain free-cash-flow positive after the capex increase will keep repurchasing stock.
In aggregate, S&P 500 free cash flow is set to fall because of the size of capex. That may interfere with buyback plans and would strengthen the headwind from positive equity supply.
risk_factors: Falling S&P 500 free cash flow from heavy capex could reduce buybacks and so remove the main offset to new equity supply.
Debt financing is becoming more expensive for hyperscalers, which pushes them toward more equity issuance.
Large upcoming issuance (Meta's offering, Anthropic's IPO) adds to the supply of equity.
